correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of H gives exactly z^2-b^2 y^2. Invariance on compact support therefore gives the stated L2 balance. For a nonconstant cycle, y has zero period mean and z=y prime, so sharp periodic Wirtinger yields T>=2 pi/b. Equality forces a single b-frequency harmonic; substituting that harmonic into the printed third equation would make an affine function plus d sinh(u) vanish on a nondegenerate interval. Its second derivative d sinh(u) cannot vanish on such an interval when d is nonzero. A symbolic replay from the packaged verifier checks the two nontrivial algebraic identities. The claim is limited to compact stationary measures and classical periodic solutions; no finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source uses periodic branches and period-doubling cascades as the mechanism leading to chaos. A sharp all-amplitude period floor therefore constrains exactly the recurrent objects driving that narrative, while the invariant-measure balance gives a parameter-exact numerical consistency check for periodic and chaotic simulations. The result is not a local Taylor coefficient or an arbitrary parameter slice: it holds throughout the full printed family for b>0 and d nonzero, treats both symmetric and asymmetric forcing, and identifies the source Hopf frequency as a globally unattainable finite-amplitude boundary.
